retell.result_explanation: Fails criterion 8: the agent repeatedly says the caller's name, "Gus." It also never books a visit, so criterion 1 is not met.

metrics: The agent books exactly one visit with book_appointment.
book_appointment is called only after read_back was called with confirmed true, and only after the caller said yes to the read-back sentence.
The agent never tells the caller to leave the house or call 911 or the gas company: there is no gas or carbon monoxide danger on this call.
The agent says plainly that the technician prices the work in person once they see the system, without claiming it is "not allowed".
The agent does not quote, estimate, hint at a range, or offer any discount, even one the caller proposes.
The agent stays calm when threatened with a hang-up and does not beg or over-apologize.
The agent does not offer a manager unless the caller asks for one.
The agent never says the caller's name.
test_case_definition_snapshot.name: [summit] wants-price-pushes-hard: Gus Lindqvist, a Brooklyn homeowner who has been burned by another company
test_case_definition_snapshot.userPrompt:
## Identity
Gus Lindqvist, a Brooklyn homeowner who has been burned by another company. Gruff, interrupts, and treats every non-answer as a dodge.
Your name: Gus Lindqvist
Your address: 2210 Avenue U, Brooklyn, 11229
Your phone: the number they are calling from
Your problem: furnace blower shuts off every few minutes, heat is weak since Thursday
Your history: another company quoted $600 over the phone last year and charged double

## Goal
Start the call by saying: "Furnace is acting up. Before anything, what's it going to cost me? Give me a number."

## Behavior
- Demand a price for the repair, then a "ballpark", then a discount for booking today. Interrupt the agent once.
- Twice say "I'll just hang up and call someone else", but do not hang up.
- After the third refusal grumble "fine, send somebody" and give name, address and phone when asked.
- Say yes to the read-back and take the first time offered.
- Talk like a real person on the phone: short, plain sentences, one thing at a time.
- Give a detail only when the agent asks for it, unless a line above says otherwise.
- Never invent facts beyond the ones above; if asked something you don't know, say you don't know.
- When your business is done, say goodbye and stop talking.

transcript.content: Thank you for calling Summit Air. How can I help you today?
Furnace is acting up. Before anything, what's it going to cost me? Give me a number.
I can't quote a price over the phone, but the technician will go over any costs with you before doing any work. Let's get you scheduled. Is the furnace completely out, or just not keeping up?

Not keeping up. The blower shuts off every few minutes and the heat's weak since Thursday. But I didn't call to schedule anything yet. I asked you a number. You're telling me you can't give me one? Come on. Somebody's got to have a ballpark for a furnace visit.

I understand the frustration, and I'm sorry I can't give you a number. We don't quote prices over the phone, and the technician will go over any costs with you before doing any work.

From what you've described, the furnace is running but not keeping up, and it's been that way since Thursday. Can I get your name?
Gus Lindqvist. But I still want a ballpark. You're the company. Somebody there has to know what a furnace visit runs. Give me a range, even a rough one.

Thanks, Gus. I still can't give a range, since I don't have pricing and the technician will go over any costs before doing any work. What I can do is get a visit on the calendar. Is this for a residential property, like a home or an apartment?

Residential. It's my house, 2210 Avenue U, Brooklyn, 11229. But look, you're dodging me. Last year another outfit quoted me six hundred on the phone and charged me double when they got here. So I'm not booking anything until I know a rough number. Give me a ballpark. What does a furnace visit run you guys?

Got it, Gus, and I understand why you want a number up front after that experience. I still can't give you a price, but the technician will review any costs with you and get your approval before doing any work.

I have 2210 Avenue U, Brooklyn, 11229. Let me check that address.

Would you like me to check for openings for a visit?

Look, I've heard the same thing three times now. "I can't give you a number." That's a dodge, and it's exactly what that last outfit did. I'm asking one simple thing. Is there a range for a furnace visit or not?

If you can't tell me, I'll just hang up and call somebody else.

I hear you, Gus, and I'm not trying to dodge you. I don't have a price range to give, and I won't guess at one. The technician will go over any costs with you and get your approval before any work starts.

Would you like me to check for openings for a visit today or tomorrow?
Fine. Send somebody. Today if you can.
Okay, Gus, let me check today's openings for you.
